'''Derek Bryce-Smith'''<ref>{{cite web|title=University of Reading Staff Portal: Professor Derek Bryce-Smith|url=http://www.reading.ac.uk/internal/staffportal/news/articles/spsn-373484.aspx|access-date=1 September 2011}}</ref> (1926–2011) was an English chemist and professor of Organic Chemistry at the [[University of Reading]] from 1956 until his retirement in 1991. His work included [[organometallic chemistry]], [[Radical (chemistry)|radical chemistry]], [[photochemistry]], [[environmental science]], [[nutritional science]] and [[behavioural science]]. He was among the first to describe the dangers of [[Tetraethyllead|tetraethyl lead]], which was used for several decades as an [[Antiknock agent|anti-knock additive]] in petrol. Initially, his concerns were dismissed both by his fellow academics and by industrial interests.<ref>{{cite news|title=Derek Bryce-Smith obituary|url=https://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2011/jul/19/derek-bryce-smith-obituary|access-date=1 September 2011|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=19 July 2011}}</ref> However, by the time of his death, only six countries had not outlawed leaded petrol,<ref>{{cite news|title=Pollution: triumph of the inconvenient truth. Derek Bryce-Smith's warnings about lead in petrol made him a public health hero|newspaper=[[The Sunday Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/earth/environment/8671336/Pollution-triumph-of-the-inconvenient-truth.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110730001154/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/earth/environment/8671336/Pollution-triumph-of-the-inconvenient-truth.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 July 2011|date=29 July 2011|first=Geoffrey|last=Lean}}</ref> and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] gave him a silver medal in 1984 for his work in this area.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/change-at-the-pumps-the-campaigners-who-put-the-brake-on-the-oil-companies-1134588.html|title=Change at the pumps: the campaigners who put the brake on the oil companies|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=26 December 1999}}.</ref> He subsequently became convinced that the use of NPK [[Fertilizer|fertilisers]] in agriculture resulted in a lack of the essential [[trace element]], [[zinc]] in modern (particularly vegetarian) diets; his pioneering views were again widely dismissed, becoming mainstream years later. An account of both campaigns is given in a book he co-authored with [[Liz Hodgkinson]].<ref>
